rule_objections: Rule is explicit and sound for anchors: aliases and keys excluded. Since GitLab CI hidden jobs (`.default-ruby-variables`) are the real 'definitions' referred to by `extends:`, but they are plain keys, they are only `configuration` symbols; a developer cannot ask for them as definitions. Arguable but consistent with the stated rule.

tests.yml (610 lines, a mapping table: `mapping: - source: ... test: ...`) legitimately has 0 anchors, and counts only 2 configuration symbols for 610 lines because the config analyser records only mapping keys, not sequence-item keys.
findings: Against the stated rule: 10 anchors expected (9 in .gitlab-ci.yml, 1 in Dependency-Scanning.v2.gitlab-ci.yml), 10 extracted as `variable`, named without '&', on the right lines; 0 missed, 0 spurious. Shell `&&` / `&` in script blocks were not mistaken for anchors. All parse ok.
Totals are dominated by the separate config analyser (not counted against the rule): 2 / 128 / 155 `configuration` symbols vs 10 anchors.
Sample is thin for anchors: only 10 in three files, and none in `<<: *alias` merge-key form beyond the aliases themselves (aliases correctly not recorded).
Text search works: `search more` (a word taken from comment text) finds both files that contain it.
not_done: No YAML with anchors inside flow collections / sequences (`- &x`) was available in these three files.
